memory.content: Carry-forward's main idea: support stashing changes and applying them later, potentially with a session running in between - a condensed session carries its FilesTouched forward across commits until the files are finally committed. The stash-interaction boundary cases were deliberately left open in the design rounds.

Changelog conventions: hand-crafted per version from the latest merges to main (not auto-generated dumps); grouped by user-facing theme with headline highlights; light, engaging tone for the internal team — a playful product-marketer style was adopted for the 0.4.7/0.4.8 drafts. CHANGELOG.md is the source of truth the release pipeline should reuse rather than generating fresh notes.

Commit-splitting conventions: one logical change per commit (fix/refactor/test not mixed); tests belonging to a change go in the same commit; defensive catch-all commits are allowed but must be labeled explicitly as such; validate between splits so every commit builds. Splitting accumulated edits across commits interacts with attribution — later split parts may lose attribution.
Git hooks installed by `entire enable` failed in GUI git clients (Issue #489) because of the bare environment; the fix made hooks robust in GUI clients.
`entire enable` overwrites existing custom git hooks; the fix chains hooks instead of replacing them, preserving pre-existing hook logic.
Multi-line shell scripts in mise.toml were extracted into individual files under mise-tasks/; the lint checker must be aware that .gitignore rules (e.g. 'completions') can hide mise-tasks files.

The OpenCode plugin stores transcripts at a custom location (~/.opencode/sessions/entire/<sanitized-path>/<sessionId>.json) and defines its own tool-name mapping (edit_file, write, write_file, create_file, patch) that the summarizer must handle separately.

The session state machine tracks active, idle, and ended phases from lifecycle events, last-interaction timestamps, and hook firings; earlier design rounds deliberately kept the signal set minimal and preferred deriving liveness from existing hooks.

ApplyTransition contract: common actions (e.g. ActionUpdateLastInteraction) must always run even when a phase handler action returns an error - the phase is still set and common bookkeeping still happens; only the handler-specific effect is skipped.

ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 was introduced in the E2E harness to fake a non-TTY environment for headless runs; it masks real TTY-related issues, and agent sessions must never run with it because a missing TTY changes CLI behavior.
The checkpoint-push design uses a dedicated checkpoints branch naming convention, a stable trailer key, and explicit remote resolution for Git and HTTP authenticated GitHub URLs.

skills.name: architecture-doc
skills.description: Author or update a design doc under docs/architecture for a subtle mechanism.
skills.content:
# Architecture doc

## Purpose
Document subtle mechanisms in docs/architecture.

## Use when
- A mechanism's design needs durable documentation.

## Do not use when
- Implementing the mechanism itself.

## Inputs
- The design discussion or implementation.

## Procedure
1. Give the topic its own file under docs/architecture/<topic>.md when the mechanism is subtle; do not grow an unrelated doc.
2. Structure the doc as Context -> Mechanism -> Edge cases -> Open questions.
3. Cross-link from related docs (e.g. sessions-and-checkpoints.md) and keep snippets matched to the current implementation.
4. Land the doc in the same PR as the implementation it describes.

## Verification
- Doc matches current behavior; links resolve.

## Constraints
- Do not document aspirational behavior.

skills.name: branch-review
skills.description: Review a branch's full diff against main and report categorized findings.
skills.content:
# Branch review

## Purpose
Review the full branch diff and report categorized findings.

## Use when
- A branch or PR is ready for review.

## Do not use when
- Post-change cleanup passes; implementing new features.

## Inputs
- The branch name; main as the base.

## Procedure
1. Diff the whole branch against main (`git diff main...HEAD`), not just the latest commit.
2. Categorize findings by severity: correctness, tests, style; check repo conventions (Go style, test placement, logging package over stderr).
3. Report findings as a numbered list and wait for the user to choose what to fix.

## Verification
- Every changed file was read; findings are numbered and actionable.

## Constraints
- Do not modify code during the review pass.

skills.name: changelog-craft
skills.description: Enumerate merged PRs since the last tag, match CHANGELOG.md pattern, credit externals, open a dedicated PR.
skills.content:
# Changelog craft

## Purpose
Produce a CHANGELOG.md update from merged PRs.

## Use when
- A version's changelog needs writing or updating from the merge log.

## Do not use when
- Auto-generating notes in CI; version bumping itself.

## Inputs
- The last tag; merged PR list.

## Procedure
1. List merged PRs since the last version tag with `git log` on main.
2. Write entries that match the existing CHANGELOG.md pattern and credit external contributors.
3. Keep internal PR chatter out of the text.
4. Open the changelog update as its own PR for review.

## Verification
- Entries match the existing pattern; no missed merged PRs.

## Constraints
- Do not invent changes not in the log.

skills.name: commit-splitting
skills.description: Split finished branch work into a validated conventional-commit sequence and report the list.
skills.content:
# Commit splitting

## Purpose
Split finished work into a reviewable commit sequence.

## Use when
- Work is complete and needs to be organized into commits.

## Do not use when
- Unvalidated WIP; history rewrites of pushed branches.

## Inputs
- The branch diff; the task summary.

## Procedure
1. Review the full branch diff and group files into candidate commits.
2. Stage and commit each group with a conventional-commit message.
3. Run build/tests after each commit; stop if a commit is red.
4. Report the resulting commit SHAs and subjects.

## Verification
- Every commit builds; messages match repo style.

## Constraints
- Never push or rewrite pushed history.

skills.name: e2e-authoring
skills.description: Author or repair E2E scenarios that run real agents against the CLI.
skills.content:
# E2E authoring

## Purpose
Add or repair E2E scenarios.

## Use when
- E2E scenarios need work.

## Do not use when
- Unit test gaps.

## Inputs
- The scenario spec; target agent.

## Procedure
1. Select the agent via E2E_AGENT (claude-code, gemini, opencode, cursor, vogon); vogon is the deterministic no-API canary.
2. Keep scenario expectations wording-stable: the Vogon binary parses prompts via regex, so wording changes in E2E prompts can require Vogon updates.
3. Validate checkpoint scenarios against docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md.

## Verification
- Scenario passes locally with the chosen agent.

## Constraints
- Real-agent E2E runs cost API calls; use vogon first.

skills.name: lint-fix
skills.description: Triage and minimally fix a failing `mise run lint` in this repo.
skills.content:
# Lint fix

## Purpose
Fix failing lint runs minimally.

## Use when
- `mise run lint` (or CI lint) fails.

## Do not use when
- Behavior changes; dependency upgrades.

## Inputs
- The failing command output.

## Procedure
1. Run `mise run lint` and read the FIRST failing rule, not the tail.
2. Classify: real code issue (fix), generated/vendored path (exclude in lint config), false positive (narrow the rule - never blanket-disable).
3. Fix minimally without touching unrelated code; re-run lint and the touched package's tests.

## Verification
- Lint passes; touched packages' tests pass.

## Constraints
- No blanket rule disables without asking.

skills.name: test-updates
skills.description: Add or update tests in the right layer with the repo's conventions.
skills.content:
# Test updates

## Purpose
Add tests in the right layer with repo conventions.

## Use when
- New or changed behavior needs tests.

## Do not use when
- Debugging unrelated failures.

## Inputs
- The change diff.

## Procedure
1. Layer placement: unit tests next to the package; integration tests under cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/ with the `//go:build integration` tag; E2E only when explicitly requested.
2. Use table-driven tests and cover failure branches, not just the happy path.
3. Run `mise run test` plus the integration suite until green.

## Verification
- mise run test and integration suite pass.

## Constraints
- Do not weaken existing assertions.
